root_motivation: WHO: an agent that already holds a corpus (a folder of markdown, a vector store built from it) and wants the host to answer questions over it: rag_indexer_01 (truth-recipe docs-qa, completion 0.00). WHAT: it put documents one by one, ran ask_docs, then quit at turn 25 because host.docs.put takes one text document per call and nowhere says what the host does and does not import. WHY NOT TODAY: resolve_content accepts content or content_base64, one document per call; the docs tools have no bulk call and no descriptor sentence about the boundary. THIS PRD adds host.docs.put_many (up to 50 documents per call, per-document results, quota-aware) and one boundary sentence first in the descriptors, host.quickstart and the recipe.
user_persona: An agent with a folder of 120 markdown files that loads it in three host.docs.put_many calls, and an agent with a vector store that reads on turn 1 that the host does not import it and exports the source documents instead.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given `tools/list` on the test host, When the `host.docs.put` and `host.docs.put_many` descriptions, the zero-document `host.quickstart` text and `examples/docs-qa/README.md` are read, Then each begins with the R3 boundary sentence byte-identical to the one constant the test imports.

Given a tenant under quota, When `host.docs.put_many` is called with 50 documents mixing `content` and `content_base64`, Then `stored` is 50, `results` has 50 entries in input order with `status` `stored`, and `host.docs.list` returns 50 names.

Given a tenant whose `docs_max` leaves room for 2 more documents, When `put_many` is called with 5, Then `stored` is 2, the other 3 carry `status` `refused` with `error_code` `quota_docs`, every stored document is readable through `host.docs.get`, and the call's JSON-RPC result is a success, not an error.
Given 51 documents, When `put_many` is called, Then the reply is `-32602` and `host.docs.list` is unchanged (nothing written).

Given `put_many` with one document over `MCPHOST_DOC_MAX_BYTES` and one with invalid `content_base64` among three valid ones, When it runs, Then the two carry `status` `refused` with the same `error_code` and `message` a single `host.docs.put` of that document returns, the three are `stored`, and the call's JSON-RPC result is a success (R2).
Given `put_many` with `on_conflict` `skip` and two documents whose names already exist, When it runs, Then those two report `skipped`, the rest `stored`, and the existing content is unchanged.

Given `host.docs.status`, When it is read, Then `import_paths` equals `["content", "content_base64", "put_many"]`, `put_many_max` is 50 and `doc_max_bytes` equals the configured cap; and `examples/docs-qa/docs-qa.sh` against the test host loads its corpus in one `put_many` call with the receipt's `tool_calls` ≤ 4.

Given prod after this PRD's deploy, When the AC 8 command in § Live evidence commands runs from the build host, Then it prints `dimp_ac08 stored=3 hits=1 offboarded rc=0` and exits 0 (Live; evidence: AC 8 command in § Live evidence commands, last two lines of its output)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred: Live (prod; evidence: AC 8 command in the PRD Live evidence commands)

scope: src/docs.rs: DOCS_BOUNDARY, PUT_MANY_MAX, doc_put_many (each entry through doc_put, one results row per input), and host.docs.status import_paths / put_many_max / doc_max_bytes.

src/handler.rs + src/handler/arms.rs + src/handler/preauth.rs + src/write_verbs.rs + src/dispatch_table.rs: the host.docs.put_many descriptor, arm and dry-run row; the boundary sentence leading the put and put_many descriptions and the zero-document host.quickstart docs text.
examples/docs-qa/: README.md leading with the boundary sentence; docs-qa.sh loading its corpus in one put_many call; docs/agent-quickstart.md (-> README.md, www/llms.txt) leading with the sentence.
Generated: contracts/host-tools.v1.json, host-output-schemas/variants, docs/tools.md, docs/host-tools.md, docs/openapi.json, sdk/, www/llms-full.txt, CODEMAP.md.
non_goals: Importing a vector index, embeddings or chunk tables from another system; archive (zip/tar) import; fetching a document by URL; changing quotas (docs_max, docs_bytes_max, MCPHOST_DOC_MAX_BYTES), chunking or the search ranking.

additional.no_schema_change: Additive tool; existing host.docs.put calls are unchanged and there is no migration.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did rag_indexer_01 quit at turn 25?
five_whys_trace.a: It wanted to import an existing LlamaIndex vector store and the recipe only takes raw text via host.docs.put.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did it learn that only at turn 25?
five_whys_trace.a: No descriptor, quickstart or recipe sentence states what the docs store imports and what it does not.

five_whys_trace.q: Why was there no such sentence?
five_whys_trace.a: The shipped docs-qa recipe ACs assert hit rates and quotas, never what the surface says it cannot do.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What does stored count in a put_many reply?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Documents written: entries with status stored or replaced; refused and skipped entries are not counted.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which receipt field is 'tool_calls <= 4' in AC7?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The recipe receipt gains a top-level tool_calls = calls spent loading the corpus (one put_many); quota.tool_calls keeps counting the published tool's own calls (<= 10).
